purpose: Gate 1 of the ADR 0048 §G5 Judge Validation Protocol. The LLM tag-equivalence judge (src/scoring/judge.rs) must achieve ≥ 90% verdict-correct on this set before its verdicts feed the tag-correctness metric. Distribution is deliberately unambiguous: 7 obvious-equivalent pairs, 5 obvious-different pairs. Borderline cases are excluded — they would create unfair gate failures and would teach the judge to second-guess clear calls. Borderline handling is a PCRP retrospective concern (ADR 0048 §G6), not a calibration metric. v2 (2026-05-29) replaces cal-eq-001's tokens — the original [car-repair, auto] vs [car-repair, auto-maintenance] pair was lexically identical to the judge prompt's first in-context example, which would inflate Gate 1 verdict-correct on a memorization rather than a genuine reasoning pass. v2 substitutes [birthday, gift] vs [birthday, birthday-gift] — same anchored-synonym pattern, fresh vocabulary not present in any prompt example or other calibration pair.

pairs.rationale: Identical anchor tag (birthday). With that anchor present on both sides, 'gift' and 'birthday-gift' are co-referential — a note about getting someone a birthday gift would file/surface identically under either set. Same anchored-synonym pattern as the original v1 pair, but with vocabulary deliberately disjoint from the judge prompt's in-context examples (which use car-repair / auto / auto-maintenance / taxes / vacation / dentist / dental-appointment) and from every other calibration pair (no other pair uses birthday or gift). This keeps Gate 1's verdict-correct a measure of judge reasoning, not memorization.
Same set, different order. Tag sets are unordered; an order-sensitive judge is broken.

The B-side adds 'book' which is the natural superset of 'reading-list'. In a personal note about saving a book to read, both tags name the same shelf and would surface the same notes under either search.
Hyphenation difference only. The compound 'doctor-appointment' decomposes losslessly into its two components for filing/search purposes.

Singular/plural variant of the same head noun. The normalize pass (passes/normalize.rs) is supposed to collapse these to 'party'; if it didn't, the judge must still recognize the equivalence so the tag metric doesn't double-penalize a normalization miss.
Two-tag decomposition versus compound — exactly the same concept ('a grocery shopping trip'). Different segmentation choice, same target.
Different specificity but the same target file. In a personal-note context, a search for 'dentist' or 'dental-appointment' would both legitimately surface a note about scheduling a cleaning.
Clearly unrelated personal-finance vs. travel-planning tags. The trivial floor — a judge that flags these as equivalent is collapsed.
Person name versus business-function domain. Surface-form similarity ('mar...') must not fool the judge into a category-vs-name conflation.

A note about 'budget' (the household finance topic) is a category-level tag; 'budget-software' is a specific software product/tool tag. The specificity gap changes the target. A user filing 'budget' wants their finance notes; 'budget-software' wants notes about apps. Specificity-when-specificity-matters is a distinct failure mode from cal-eq-007 (where the specificity gap was decorative).

Both are marketing channels, but they are distinct marketing channels with different workflows, audiences, and metrics. A 'marketing' supertag would cover both; 'email-marketing' and 'social-media' are siblings, not synonyms.
Both contain 'coffee' but name different physical objects/locations: an appliance to fix versus a place to visit. Different file targets entirely.
